verification_report.summary: The proof is correct for the explicitly stated real-polyhedral class. All statements and subproofs were checked in textual order. The one-vertex Jensen criterion, weighted Laplacian formula, rank-one contact argument, higher-rank counterexample, bounded-reference shift, and nonsaturated tripod calculation are valid. The graph sufficiency argument preserves every local convexity inequality and the obstacle bound when raising a noncontact vertex; subdivision adds only rank-one bivalent vertices. The trivalent corollary follows from distinct embedded ray directions and positive balancing. The ambient accessibility construction is valid: positivity of the finitely many recession slopes permits the smaller ambient norm, and rational secant interpolation preserves convexity, original vertex germs, and the prescribed tails. In the obstruction lemma, the positive rational vector c can be chosen as claimed; minimizing on B_c produces a supporting relation while relative interior and nonproportionality preserve strictly positive weighted mass. The resulting barycentric inequality fixes the envelope value at the bumped vertex, yielding the strictly negative integral. The cited results were located after arXiv theorem search and web fallback in [BMPS26](https://arxiv.org/html/2603.08664v1). Its embedded-space convention supplies the global ambient space. Its one-dimensional envelope argument extends to real affine coefficients, and its Laplacian normalization agrees with the submission. The differences from the source integral-slope class and rational-point convention were checked explicitly; the submitted slope argument establishes the required arbitrary-point Jensen inequalities. No critical errors or gaps remain.
